question.worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)=(t-1)({t}^{2}+2),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =(1)({t}^{2}+2)+(t-1)(2t) \\  & =({t}^{2}+2)+2t(t-1),\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(-1)=({(-1)}^{2}+2)+2(-1)((-1)-1)=7.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(8-{t}^{2}),$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=-\frac{2t}{8-{t}^{2}},
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(-1)=-\frac{2\cdot (-1)}{8-{(-1)}^{2}}=\frac{2}{7}.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(-1) & =⟨{x}^{′}(-1),\,{y}^{′}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨7,\,\frac{2}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
